findings.where: apps/web/messages/en.json:6294 (`IntakeBatch.stopping.title`), rendered by apps/web/components/documents/intake-batch-card.tsx:221 and locked in by apps/web/components/documents/intake-batch-card.test.tsx:188-193
findings.what: The value shipped for `IntakeBatch.stopping.title` is `"正在停止 · Stopping this batch"` — a literal Chinese phrase concatenated onto the English string in the sole locale file, `en.json`. `git show origin/main:apps/web/messages/en.json | grep -cP '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]'` returns 0: before this branch the file contains zero CJK characters anywhere, so this is not an established convention of the file, it is the first and only instance. The house docs (DECISIONS.md, brief-636.md) themselves mix Chinese prose for the *owner-facing* internal planning text (a documented convention for that document class), and the brief's own English translation of the same UI-contract line reads "Show stopping and explain that already admitted operations are finishing; reveal completed receipts" — no Chinese. The implementer appears to have copied the Chinese descriptive phrase from DECISIONS.md's Q6 ruling ("the accountant sees 正在停止 on the press") into the literal product string instead of treating it as internal shorthand, and then wrote a test (`intake-batch-card.test.tsx:193`, `assert.match(text, /正在停止/)`) that locks the mistake in as intended behaviour.
findings.evidence: `grep -n '正在停止' apps/web/messages/en.json` -> line 6294 (`"title": "正在停止 · Stopping this batch"`). `grep -n '正在停止|stopping' apps/web/components/documents/intake-batch-card.tsx` -> line 221 (`<StateBanner ... title={t("stopping.title")}>`) renders it unconditionally whenever `ready.batch.state === "cancelling"`. `git show origin/main:apps/web/messages/en.json | grep -cP '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]'` -> 0 (no other CJK content anywhere in the base file).
findings.fix: Drop the Chinese phrase from the shipped `en.json` string (e.g. `"Stopping this batch"`) and drop the corresponding assertion in intake-batch-card.test.tsx; if the product genuinely wants a bilingual accountant-facing surface, that is a locale/i18n decision for a separate ticket, not a hand-inserted phrase inside the single `en` locale file.

findings.where: apps/web/components/documents/intake-batch-card.tsx:120 (doc comment) vs :304 (`{!readOnly && !terminal ? (...Cancel button...) : null}`); mounted with `readOnly` at apps/web/components/firm/documents/unassigned-sources.tsx:110-118
findings.what: brief-636.md's Web section is explicit: the card is mounted "on `/documents` (in `components/firm/documents/unassigned-sources.tsx`, read-only apart from Cancel)" — i.e. every other affordance is disabled on the firm leaf EXCEPT Cancel, which must remain reachable. The component's own prop doc-comment restates this verbatim (`/** The firm leaf mounts this read-only apart from Cancel. */`, line 120). But the only place `readOnly` is consulted in the whole component is the single line that renders the Cancel trigger button: `{!readOnly && !terminal ? (...) : null}` (line 304). Passing `readOnly` (as `unassigned-sources.tsx` does, unconditionally) therefore HIDES the one control the brief says must stay — Cancel is completely unreachable on the firm `/documents` leaf, the opposite of the stated contract. The firm-leaf mount also wires `onCancelled={() => { void sources.reload(); }}` (unassigned-sources.tsx:117), which is dead code given the trigger that would fire it can never be reached — corroborating that Cancel was meant to work there and the boolean is inverted, not a deliberate scope cut. Neither `intake-batch-card.test.tsx` nor `unassigned-sources.test.tsx` nor the Playwright walk (`intake-batch-walk.spec.ts`, which only ever visits `/clients/:id/documents`) exercises the firm leaf's `readOnly` mount at all, so nothing caught the inversion. The final report (`636-final.md:75`) restates the surface as merely "read-only" (dropping "apart from Cancel") without flagging that as a departure from the brief's binding text, which the house's own evidence-law convention (state a departure, never let it be silent) requires.
findings.evidence: `grep -n readOnly apps/web/components/documents/intake-batch-card.tsx` -> only 3 lines: the prop declaration (109/121) and the gate at 304, which is the Cancel button's sole visibility condition — no other element in the file checks `readOnly`. `grep -n -i cancel apps/web/components/firm/documents/unassigned-sources.test.tsx` -> no matches; `grep -n '/documents' apps/web/e2e/intake-batch-walk.spec.ts` shows every `page.goto` targets `/clients/${CLIENT_ID}/documents`, never the firm `/documents` leaf.
findings.fix: Either add a second condition so the Cancel trigger renders when `readOnly && !terminal` too (matching "read-only apart from Cancel"), or, if the firm leaf was deliberately narrowed to fully read-only during implementation, say so explicitly as a stated departure in the final report and drop the now-dead `onCancelled` wiring and the stale doc comment. Add a unit or walk cell that mounts the firm leaf and asserts Cancel's actual visibility, so either behaviour is provably intentional going forward.
